name: analyze_video
description: Understand an existing video or screen recording using timestamped sampled frames and optional audio transcription. Accepts a Jarvis Stash reference or allowed local MP4, WebM, MOV, MKV, AVI, M4V, or MPEG file. Works with silent videos. Use for explaining screen recordings, demonstrations, visible events, comparing a video with documents, and questions about a particular time range. Inspects up to six frames per request; brief events between samples may be missed. Defaults to the first 300 seconds, and can inspect another interval up to 300 seconds with start_seconds/end_seconds. Returns visual findings, exact sampled timestamps, selected interval, transcript status, source references, and explicit coverage warnings. The source file is retained by its existing Stash policy; temporary frames/audio are not saved. For follow-up or Canvas, preserve the exact source_ref and timestamp/coverage metadata. Remote URLs must first be downloaded into Stash using the appropriate existing download tool.

availability.setup_hint: Install FFmpeg (including ffprobe) on the Jarvis host and select a vision-capable model.

source.description: Existing video as stash://space_id/file_id or an allowed local file path. Remote URLs are not accepted.

question.description: What to learn from the recording. Default describes visible events and spoken content.

start_seconds.description: Start of the selected interval, in seconds from the beginning. Default 0.

end_seconds.description: Exclusive end in seconds. Must be within the video and at most 300 seconds after start. Defaults to the next 300 seconds or end of video.

include_audio.description: Transcribe audio from the selected interval when present. Default true. Set false for visual-only analysis; audio is then explicitly marked skipped.
